events.text: Halfway through class, somebody's phone plays a video of Kelly face-planting at cheer practice. The room erupts. Kelly goes very still. Every head turns to see what the new kid does.

choices.label: Laugh along. It IS funny.
choices.result: You laugh. Everyone laughs. Kelly looks right at you, and files you somewhere permanent.

choices.label: "Put it away. That's low."
choices.result: The laughter dies awkwardly. Kelly doesn't thank you. She does look at you a second longer than necessary.

choices.label: Stare at your desk until it's over.
choices.result: You become extremely interested in a scratch on the desk. History will not remember this.

events.text: Coach Byrne blows the whistle. "Laps. Until I get bored." She does not get bored.
events.result: Your legs file a formal complaint.

events.text: Dodgeball. The Upside-Down has nothing on a gym full of teenagers with rubber balls.
events.result: You dodge most of them. Most.

events.text: Surprise fitness test. Coach has a clipboard and no mercy.
events.successText: You finish strong. Coach nods once, which from her is a standing ovation.
events.failText: You finish. Technically. Coach writes something down.

events.text: Partner stretches. You're stuck with {partner}.

choices.label: Make small talk
choices.result: You talk about nothing. It's nice.

choices.label: Push the stretch (and them)
choices.result: Somebody's hamstring makes a noise. Progress.

events.text: The rope climb. Somebody waxed the rope. Somebody always waxes the rope.
events.successText: You make it to the top and ring the little bell. Nobody claps, but you know.
events.failText: You make it a third of the way up, then very quickly all the way down.

events.text: Kelly runs the squad through a routine at the edge of the gym, very loudly, during your class.

choices.label: Watch, honestly impressed
choices.result: She notices you noticing. She pretends she didn't.

choices.label: Heckle
choices.result: Dex laughs. Kelly does not.

events.text: Coach Byrne keeps you after class. "You've got more in you than that. I've seen it." She shows you how to plant your feet and put your whole body into a hit.
events.result: Your next punch feels like it has a mortgage.

events.text: Coach Byrne catches three people slacking without turning around. You stop slacking without having started.
Ms. G explains momentum for ten minutes, then momentum as a metaphor for forty.
events.result: You understand momentum. And, briefly, yourself.

events.text: "Right, right, the assignment. Anyway, entropy—" The lesson departs for parts unknown.
events.result: You learn three things, none of them on the test.

events.text: Pop quiz: a ball rolls off a desk. How fast is it going when Ms. G stops talking about it?
events.successText: You show your work. Ms. G draws a smiley face that is also a vector diagram.
events.failText: Your answer is 'fast'. Partial credit for vibes.

events.text: Lab partners: you and {partner}, a cart, a ramp, and a stopwatch that only works if you hold it at an angle.

choices.label: Let them run it
choices.result: They're good at this. You say so. They light up.

choices.label: Take the measurements yourself
choices.result: Precise. Slightly bossy. Precise.

events.text: The giant demonstration pendulum swings back. Ms. G says 'don't flinch, trust the physics.'
events.successText: You don't flinch. It stops an inch from your nose. Physics: trusted.
events.failText: You flinch into the pendulum's path. Physics: right, you: wrong.

events.text: Theo whispers a correction to Ms. G's equation, then looks horrified that he said it out loud.

choices.label: Back him up
choices.result: Ms. G checks it. Theo was right. He goes pink.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.result: Ms. G carries on. Theo sinks into his hoodie.

events.text: Ms. G grabs you after class. "You see it too, don't you? Force isn't a push. It's an argument with the universe." She sketches a line on the board that you can almost feel.
events.result: You can see straight lines in the air now. Is that normal? (It's not.)

events.text: Ms. G mutters about 'statistical outliers' while grading, eyeing two names on the roster you can't quite read.
Titration. One drop too many and the whole flask turns the color of regret.
Something in the back cabinet smells like a penny that's seen things.
events.result: You identify it. Nobody should be able to identify that.

events.text: Quiz: balance the equation before Ms. G finishes her coffee.
events.successText: Balanced. Ms. G raises her mug to you.
events.failText: Unbalanced, much like the lab stool.

events.text: Paired with {partner} for a lab with the warning label 'probably fine'.

choices.label: Follow the procedure exactly
choices.result: It is, in fact, probably fine.

choices.label: Improvise a little
choices.result: Your eyebrows survive. Mostly. {partner} thinks you're hilarious.

events.text: A beaker tips toward your sleeve in slow motion.
events.successText: You catch it. The lab applauds, then remembers to be cool.
events.failText: Your sleeve dissolves a little. So does your dignity.

events.text: Penny finishes the lab first, then explains, loudly, why everyone else did it wrong.

choices.label: Challenge her result
choices.result: She respects it. She'll never say so. She respects it.

choices.label: Ask her to show you
choices.result: She shows you. Slowly. Like you're a substitute teacher.

events.text: "Some reactions don't stop when they should," Ms. G says, not looking at you. "Some of them leave a mark on the room itself." She writes three words on the board and erases them before anyone else comes in.
events.result: Transmutation. Vitality. Corrosion. You'll remember them.

events.text: The Earth Science Teacher passes around a rock. "This one is four hundred million years old." It looks it.
Today's forecast, in a nature-documentary voice: "And here we see the town's weather, behaving... not quite naturally." The board shows this week's readings.
events.result: Something about the numbers on the board tells you what tonight will feel like.

events.text: Quiz: name the three types of rock and one emotion they make you feel.
events.successText: Igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic, and awe. Full marks.

events.text: Field notes with {partner}. You're both supposed to be looking at clouds.

choices.label: Name the clouds
choices.result: That one's a dog. That one's a worse dog. {partner} laughs.

choices.label: Actually take notes
choices.result: Cumulus, building. Weather's changing tonight.

events.text: Sam is asleep on his textbook. The teacher is heading his way.

choices.label: Nudge him awake
choices.result: He wakes up, mutters 'five more minutes', and answers the question perfectly.

choices.label: Let fate decide
choices.result: Fate decides. Sam answers the question in his sleep. Correctly.

events.text: A mini field trip to the edge of the park. The ground near the woods is... warm?
events.successText: You notice the frost pattern on the grass is shaped like a hand. You do not mention this.
events.failText: You step in a cold patch that goes ankle-deep. It wasn't there a second ago.

events.text: "You've noticed it too," the teacher says quietly. "The weather here keeps a schedule. Hot weeks. Cold weeks. Like something's breathing." They hand you an old notebook of readings.
events.result: Their handwriting gets shakier toward the back.

events.text: Birdhouses. Mr. J says 'nice, nice, just don't lose a finger' eleven times.
events.result: Your birdhouse is structurally a birdhouse.

events.text: Mr. J fires up the little forge in the corner. The heat feels like it's listening.
Safety quiz. Mr. J holds up a tool. You must name it and say how not to die using it.
events.successText: Correct, and all ten fingers agree.
events.failText: You call the chisel 'the pokey one'. Not wrong.

events.text: You and {partner} share a workbench and one working clamp.

choices.label: Let them have the clamp
choices.result: Generosity, in clamp form.

choices.label: Build something together
choices.result: It's a shelf. It's a bad shelf. It's YOUR bad shelf.

events.text: The bandsaw makes a noise bandsaws should not make.
events.successText: You hit the kill switch. Mr. J gives you a thumbs up from under a table.
events.failText: A splinter the size of a pencil finds your palm.

events.text: You open the wrong cabinet. Inside: blueprints for something with too many gears and a label that just says 'TOWN'. Mr. J closes it, calmly. "...you weren't supposed to see that yet."

choices.label: "See what?"
choices.result: He nods. You're good at this.

choices.label: "What is it?"
choices.result: "Later." He means it. That's the scary part.

events.text: Mr. J shows you how to wrap a spell around a tool so it holds, like tempering steel. "The blacksmith taught me that. Don't tell him I told you."
events.result: Your hammer hums for a full minute afterward.

events.text: Mr. Mustard: "Project from the diaphragm. The structure is inside you, my guy."
Improv. You're a lighthouse keeper. Your scene partner is a lighthouse. It goes surprisingly well.
Cold read: a monologue about a lost sandwich. Mr. Mustard sits back, unbothered.
events.successText: Someone in the back row tears up over the sandwich.
events.failText: You read the stage directions out loud. Mr. Mustard calls it 'a choice'.

events.text: Scene work with {partner}. The scene is 'two people who need the same parking spot'.

choices.label: Let them win the scene
choices.result: They get the parking spot. They're thrilled.

choices.label: Go big
choices.result: You commit. You commit hard. There's polite applause.

events.text: The stage trapdoor is supposed to be locked.
events.successText: You step around it like a pro.
events.failText: It was not locked. You are briefly, and then permanently, a theater legend.

events.text: Priya gives you a 'note' on your performance. It's three pages long. Color-coded.

choices.label: Argue the note
choices.result: She lights up. You've given her a worthy opponent.

choices.label: Take the note
choices.result: It's... actually a good note.

events.text: Mr. Mustard turns the stage lights on you and walks away. "Stand there until it stops being scary." It takes a while. Then the light feels like yours.
events.result: Being looked at is a skill. You have it now. A little.

events.text: Rebuttal drills. Mr. Mustard agrees with everyone, which is somehow the hardest thing to argue with.
Resolved: this town should have more than one deli. The room nearly riots on Gary's behalf.
Timed round. Two minutes to argue that cereal is a soup.
events.successText: The judges are convinced. They're also uncomfortable.
events.failText: You argue that soup is a cereal. Points for courage.

events.text: You're on a team with {partner}. Your opponents have binders.

choices.label: Back up their points
choices.result: You make them look brilliant. They notice.

choices.label: Take the lead
choices.result: You win. They wanted to win. Complicated.

events.text: Baxter objects to the objection to his objection. Mr. Mustard says 'okay'.

choices.label: Side with Baxter
choices.result: "Finally. Someone with SENSE."

choices.label: Side with Priya
choices.result: Priya smiles the smile of a shark.

events.text: You argue so hard you nearly lose your voice.
events.successText: Your voice holds. So does your point.
events.failText: Your last rebuttal comes out as a squeak.

events.text: "An argument is a binding," Mr. Mustard says, very calmly, "You tie two ideas together until one of them can't move." He means it literally. You can tell.
Mitochondria, the powerhouse of the cell, explained by a teacher who will not look at the diagram of a heart.
The Biology Teacher describes a paper cut as 'a superficial epidermal discontinuity' and has to sit down.
Quiz: label the parts of a frog. The frog is, thankfully, a drawing.
events.successText: Every label in the right place. The teacher is visibly relieved.
events.failText: You label the frog 'Gerald'. Not technically wrong.

events.text: Microscope work with {partner}. One of you has to focus. The other has to not sneeze.

choices.label: You sneeze-guard, they focus
choices.result: Teamwork. Beautiful, sneeze-free teamwork.

choices.label: You take the eyepiece
choices.result: There's something in the sample that waves at you. You decide it didn't.

events.text: Dissection day. The teacher hands you the scalpel and leaves the room 'for air'.
events.successText: Steady hands. You finish and clean up. The teacher returns, pale, and gives you an A.
events.failText: You get queasy and nick your thumb.

events.text: Mara's lab sketch is better than the textbook. It's also, in one corner, a drawing of something with too many eyes.

choices.label: Ask about the eyes
choices.result: "I don't know. I just see it sometimes." She closes the book.

choices.label: Compliment the frog
choices.result: She smiles at her shoes. It's a very good frog.

events.text: "Living things want to keep living," the teacher says, oddly intense. "That want is a force. Some people can... borrow it." They swallow. "Hypothetically."
Ms. Nonsense: "Pay attention. I will not repeat myself twice in one century." She repeats herself twice.
The town's founding. There's a gap in the records around a bad winter. Ms. Nonsense skips it very quickly.
Quiz: list the town's mayors in order. All of them. From memory.
events.successText: Ms. Nonsense finds no mistakes and looks personally offended.
events.failText: You list four mayors and a weatherman.

events.text: Group project with {partner}: a timeline of the town. Ms. Nonsense will grade it like a court case.

choices.label: Split the work evenly
choices.result: Fair. Efficient. Friendship-adjacent.

choices.label: Dig into the weird years
choices.result: There are a lot of 'moved away' notes in the 1980s. A LOT.

events.text: Something happens in the back row involving Sam, Baxter and a rubber band. Ms. Nonsense turns around. Nobody is doing anything.

choices.label: Cover for them
choices.result: "Those two think I don't notice. I notice."

choices.label: Stay out of it
choices.result: You learn nothing about rubber bands, and a lot about self-preservation.

events.text: Ms. Nonsense drops an enormous textbook on your desk to make a point. Your fingers are in the way of the point.
events.successText: Fingers withdrawn in time. Point received.

events.text: Ms. Nonsense keeps you after class. "I'm not telling you this because I like you." She shows you a yearbook page where every face has been cut out except one. It's the vice principal, thirty years younger.
events.result: She takes it back before you can look closer.
